To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a polypeptide can be sequenced by gas chromatography-mas spectrometry, and that this method is complementary to the Edman degradation.

the sequence of polypeptide chains can be determined by a new technique that consists of a partial hydrolysis, followed by derivatization, and gas chromatography and/or mass spectrometric analysis of the mixture of oligopeptide fragments, which can be interpreted by a computer.
the amino acid sequence analysis of polypeptide and proteins is now possible by a new method which combines partial acid hydrolysis and gas chromatography-mas spectrometry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure of biologically important proteins and peptides.
the application of combined gas chromatography mass spectrometry to the analysis of polypeptide mixtures.
the development of new methods for determining the sequence of peptides and proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined gas chromatography/mass spectrometry method is a valuable addition to the methods of protein sequencing.
the new method is a valuable supplement to the Edman degradation.
the two procedures are equally useful and that the choice between them should be made according to the specific requirements of the problem at hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for the sequence determination of polypeptides.

the new method has been developed and applied successfully to a wide variety of polypeptides, including the complete primary structures of two proteins, the 30 000 dalton subunit of the ATP synthetase from Escherichia coli and the 30 600 dalton subunit from the yeast mitochondrial ATPase.
the combined GC-MS method has the advantage of being applicable to a larger number of polypeptide samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gas chromatography-mas spectrometry (GC-MS) can provide the sequence information for polypeptides.
the new technique is capable of determining amino acid sequences of proteins of up to 40-50 residues in length.
the method is very useful for determining the sequence of peptides that cannot be sequenced by the Edman degradation.
